paragraphs.label: Μέρος Αʹ — Ἡ Ὀψία (Part A — The Evening)
paragraphs.translation: It is evening and the day has been long; night is near.
So the farmer leads the sheep from the field and carries the lamb on his shoulder. For the small lamb is weary because it has been running all day. Now it does not want to run.
So the good and strong farmer carries the lamb on his shoulder and walks along the road toward the house. The sheep follows.
The moon rises in the sky and shines beautifully upon the field and upon the river. On the road the farmer sees the moon and rejoices; for the evening is beautiful.
The farmer is weary and is about to rest in the house. For the day has been long and he wants to sleep; so he walks toward the house and arrives outside the house.
He leaves his animals outside; so he opens the door and walks into the house. The farmer is alone in the house.
But there is darkness in the house; for it is night and the farmer cannot see in the darkness. So he searches for the lamp and finds the lamp on the table.
So he lights the lamp; the lamp shines on the table and there is light in the house; there is no longer darkness.

The farmer sees bread and fruits on the table; so he rejoices and sits on the chair. For the day has been long and for a long time he has been digging the field and carrying stones. So he wants to eat and drink and rest.

So he takes the bread and eats, and the fruits. The farmer rests in the house; for he does not dig nor carry stones but eats and rests. The lamp shines on the table and there is light in the house. The moon shines outside in the sky.

Finally the farmer wants to sleep because he is very weary. For the day has been long and the toil has been long. He no longer wants to sit on the chair and remain. He has a good bed in the house. So he walks toward the bed and sleeps on the bed.

paragraphs.label: Μέρος Βʹ — Ὁ Ὕπνος (Part B — The Dream)
paragraphs.translation: The lamp still shines on the table and the moon shines outside in the sky. The farmer sleeps on his bed. And in his sleep he sees the field.
But the field is not good in the dream. For there are stones in the field — not one stone but many stones. The stones are great and hard.

The farmer sees the stones and does not rejoice. For he wants to lift and carry them out of the field. So he lifts the first stone and carries it. But there are still many stones in the field. He lifts the second stone and carries it. But there are still stones. And again he lifts and again carries.
But still many stones remain in the field; it is not possible for him to lift all the stones out of the field. The farmer is very weary and groans.

And immediately he searches for his animals in the field. But where is the lamb? He does not see it. And where is the sheep? He runs toward the sheep; but the sheep do not stay. For the sheep flee and run from the farmer.
And look! There are wolves across the river. Not one wolf but many wolves. The wolves are great and evil. The wolves see the sheep and the lamb and want to seize them.
The wolves are about to cross over the river and run into the field. The farmer also runs toward them; for he wants to save his animals from the wolves.
But look! It is not possible for him to run quickly. He wants to cry out with a great voice, but his voice is weak. And great fear takes hold of him.

And immediately he is no longer in the field but outside his house. He is about to find the door and walk into the house. But look — there is not one door but many doors! He marvels and looks toward the many doors.
He opens the first door — but there is darkness. He opens the second door — but everywhere there is darkness. Finally he opens the third door and walks into the house.

Inside the house he searches for the lamp because darkness is everywhere. For there is no light. But it is not possible to find the lamp. So he walks in the darkness and falls because he cannot see the way. And great fear takes hold of him again.
And immediately there is no longer darkness in the house. But look! Not one — but the animals are in the house: the donkey and the ox are in the house and sit on the chairs like people!
The farmer marvels greatly and looks at the animals. Suddenly the donkey says to the farmer: 'We want to eat the fruits and the bread!'
The farmer hears the voice of the donkey and marvels greatly; great fear takes hold of him again. He looks at the donkey and the ox and does not know what to do.
So he says to the donkey: 'What are you saying? For you are an animal!' The donkey again says: 'We do not have fruits nor bread; we want to eat!'
The farmer has great fear and wants to flee out of the house. He walks toward the door, but it is not possible to open it. The donkey says again: 'Bring the fruits!'
And the farmer cries out with a great voice: 'I don't want to!' And his own voice wakes him from sleep.
So he opens his eyes and sees the house; for the lamp still shines on the table and there is light in the house; there is no darkness.
He searches for the animals — and look, they are outside! He understands therefore that it was a dream and not true; so he has peace in his heart and sleeps again.
